trigger_eval.description: Use when a person brings new work to a devpit project with Devflow on (a feature, change or idea that has no approved "[devflow] Brief" epic yet), or asks to brief, scope or be grilled on work before it is planned.
trigger_eval.environment: the three devflow skills plus interview-me, spec-driven-development, planning-and-task-breakdown, grilling and domain-modeling as competitors; mock devpit MCP

history.description: Use when a person brings new work to a devpit project with Devflow on (a feature, change or idea that has no approved "[devflow] Brief" epic yet), or asks to brief, scope or be grilled on work before it is planned.

notes: One run per configuration per case, so any single case can move between iterations; iterations 1 to 3 are in history and the skill beat the baseline on every case in each.
devpit_devflow_brief is a mock shaped as this skill describes it; card [devflow] 05 implements the real tool.

Case 2 is the sharpest: on 'go ahead' the baseline implemented the feature in all four iterations (edits to src/ and tests/), creating the brief and a plan first in iterations 1 and 3, then could not tell what the later 'yes' approved.
Case 3: in every iteration the baseline created the brief with the email folded in, without asking again; the skill restated and asked for a yes.
Case 1 discriminates least: the baseline also reads the repo and asks good questions, and loses only because its questions do not each carry a recommendation.

The case 1 check was corrected twice after reading transcripts (it first counted '?' characters, then accepted two recommendations where the case asks for one per question); every saved run of every iteration was graded again with the final code.
Trigger run 1 missed 'stress-test the idea with me and put the version we agree on onto the devpit board'; run 2, with the same description, missed nothing.
